transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sofia Park (Redwood Partner Ops), Priya Raman (Astradyne Head of Partnerships), Tom Keller (Astradyne RSD), Lena Zhou (Astradyne Solutions Architect), Raj Patel (Astradyne Deal Desk)

Summary: Quick sprint to align co-sell playbook, prioritize partner-sourced pipeline, sort lead routing and incentives, and surface any legal or capacity constraints. Action items captured at end. Surface-level technical check for Dedicated vs hosted routing on top-tier deals.

Topics: playbook handoff, lead routing, co-sell credits/commission, joint executive outreach, technical validation for priority accounts, competitive positioning (Anthropic/Cohere/Vertex AI), legal/SLA flags

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know we've got a tight agenda—co-sell playbook, prioritize pipeline, and decide owners. I'll run through the playbook handoff first then Diego can cover the quickbench requirements.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Maya. Appreciate it. We have, uh, about eight opportunities we've identified that might benefit from a joint Redwood+Astradyne pitch. We'll share details after this.
[00:28] Tom: One clarification—when you say co-sell credit, what does that look like on the Redwood invoice? Do we get a referral fee or is it credit toward our MDF?
[00:35] Maya: Good q. The playbook outlines two models—referral commission on closed net new ARR, or co-commit credits that convert to partner credits you can spend on top-level deals. We'll include both examples in the spreadsheet.
[00:47] Raj: And does that require a separate contract amendment or will it sit inside the existing partner agreement?
[00:51] Sofia: Most of the initial deals can be handled under our standard partner T&Cs; for anything that needs special revenue share we'll loop in legal. We'll flag any deviation in the playbook.
[01:05] Diego: Quick technical note—some of the target accounts prefer Dedicated capacity because of data residency. We should surface the performance delta between Hosted and Dedicated so marketing and sales have talking points.
[01:18] Lena: Yes, for two of our accounts we need the VPC option and an SLA. If Dedicated has a higher unit cost what are the cost offsets?
[01:27] Maya: Good call—Diego will run a quickbench that shows latency/cost for typical LLM workloads at 2k and 8k context lengths for both Hosted vs Dedicated. We'll attach that to the playbook.
[01:39] Tom: Also, deal ownership. If Astradyne sources the lead and we bring it in, how is ACV split for quota and compensation?
[01:47] Maya: The playbook recommends a default 'originator' credit to Astradyne on closed-won and co-assignment to the Redwood AE for quota split. Exact comp details are up to your ops; we can supply the lead credit evidence from SFDC.
[02:02] Priya: Smooth. Wanted to surface one red flag—one of the prioritized accounts is in the financial services vertical and they require SOC2 plus ISO. Do you have a standard security pack?
[02:13] Sofia: Yes we updated our security pack this quarter. We'll put the SOC2 attestation and cert links into the playbook. If they need on-prem, we can discuss Private deployments but that tends to be longer lead time.
[02:28] [02:30] Diego: (murmur) I'm going to share a quick slide with the bench numbers now...
[02:35] [02:40] Diego: Ok, so host vs dedicated, here's the rough: Hosted avg 70ms p95 at 2k tokens, dedicated p95 closer to 40ms with optimized batching. Cost per 1k tokens roughly 30% higher on Dedicated before discounts; with reserved capacity the delta shrinks to around 10-12%. These are ballpark for the curated model we referenced.
[03:02] Lena: That 30% is bigger than expected. The reserved pricing is attractive though. What's the minimum commitment for reserved?
[03:10] Maya: For Dedicated we usually start at a monthly commit equivalent to X GPU-hours; Diego will include a sample commit band in the spreadsheet.
[03:19] Tom: Are there region constraints? One of the accounts wants EU-only data flow.
[03:23] Sofia: We have EU regions available for both Hosted and Dedicated; Private deployments can be air-gapped or on-prem if compliance requires it.
[03:31] Priya: Great. On the pipeline—these eight opportunities, two are near-term (P0) and five are mid-funnel P1. The P0s are in manufacturing and healthcare respectively. We want to push the manufacturing opportunity first because of a high-level sponsor.
[03:47] Maya: Let's go deal by deal. Can you name the P0s and the current owners in Astradyne's CRM?
[03:52] Priya: Sure. Deal Alpha (manufacturing) Owner: Sarah Lin; Deal Beta (healthcare) Owner: Mark Owens. I'll send contact emails after but Alpha has an exec sponsor—VP of Product—who's interested in a demo by next week.
[04:06] Maya: Perfect. We can do an initial joint demo—Diego can run the technical portion, I'll cover the commercial and co-sell angle.
[04:12] Diego: Quick note—for the demo we should confirm the model choice. If Alpha wants low-latency retrieval augmented generation, we should show the model variant with KV cache and a live doc retrieval example.
[04:24] Priya: They use an internal docs corpus, so demonstrating retrieval+generation will be high impact.
[04:29] [04:30] Tom: On enablement—what collateral will you give Astradyne SDRs? We have a 7-person biz dev team who need quick objection handling.
[04:38] Maya: We'll provide a one-pager cheat sheet, objection handling doc, and short recorded walkthrough. Also a shared playbook doc with customer red flags and escalation path.
[04:48] Priya: Can we get the cheat sheet in PPT form? Our team uses slides in outreach emails.
[04:52] Sofia: Yes, PPT and an HTML snippet for quick copy/paste.
[04:56] [05:00] Raj: Legal question: If Astradyne introduces a customer who becomes a Redwood customer directly, how do we prove attribution? SFDC notes are fine but we want something more formal.
[05:10] Maya: We'll add a lead registration form + timestamped email thread guideline. If there's any dispute, we can pull registration and activity logs from SFDC.
[05:20] Raj: Cool.
[05:22] [05:30] Diego: Back on technical: two of the targeted accounts have strict inference throughput needs—10k qps for short responses. We should decide routing policy: route to Dedicated with reserved pooling or split between Dedicated and Hosted.
[05:40] Lena: 10k qps seems high—can Redwood's autoscaling preserve latency during spikes?
[05:45] Diego: Yes, autoscaling with pre-warmed burst nodes plus smart routing helps; but reserved Dedicated capacity is the safer bet for guaranteed p95 latency. We can draft fallback policies in the ops doc.
[05:58] Tom: Any known customer objections around model hallucinations? One healthcare account is cautious.
[06:05] Maya: We recommend eval suites and guardrails; Redwood Optimize can run prompt/regression monitoring and we can include eval results in the playbook to show expected false positive rates.
[06:16] Priya: That helps. We'll ask for an eval snapshot for the healthcare POC.
[06:20] Maya: Action: Diego will produce a short eval for the sample prompt set and include recommendations for prompt-level guardrails.
[06:28] [06:30] Diego: I'll also include an embargoed sample of latency and token-cost numbers per request shape so you can model TCO.
[06:34] Priya: For joint closes, what about the co-selling motions? Do you want to run executive sponsor calls together or have Redwoods handle the SLG contact?
[06:44] Maya: Early on, we prefer a joint exec touch with both parties—helps accelerate decisioning. The playbook includes an exec touch cadence.
[06:52] Tom: If we do a joint demo next week, who owns the slide deck?
[06:56] Diego: Redwood will own the technical deck, Astradyne will own the business outcomes slide; we'll merge them.
[07:02] [07:15] Priya: Ok if I share access to an internal data sample for the demo? It's sanitized but might contain some proprietary structure.
[07:22] Diego: We can accept sanitized samples. For anything sensitive we'll use a staging VPC and ephemeral keys.
[07:30] Priya: Good.
[07:32] [07:40] Sofia: Quick ops note—we'll create a shared SFDC opportunity field flags: "Partner Originated", "Co-Sell Active", "Preferred Routing: Dedicated/Hosted". That way both of our teams can see where opportunities are.
[07:51] Raj: I'll need a doc describing the required evidence for "Partner Originated" so audits go smoothly.
[07:56] Maya: We'll send the evidence checklist.
[08:02] [08:15] Priya: About incentives—if Astradyne brings the lead and we win, is there an uplift in partner compensation if we hit a quarterly target?
[08:23] Maya: The playbook has a stretch incentive—if Astradyne-originated ARR exceeds a threshold in a quarter, we apply a bonus credit. We'll include examples.
[08:32] Tom: Do you have references from other partners doing co-sell motions? We want to show internal execs proof-of-concept.
[08:38] Maya: Yes, we have two references—one mid-market fintech and one healthcare ISV; I'll include their contact and a sanitized case study.
[08:46] [08:55] Priya: Legal/Procurement note: procurement wants a single PO flow - can Redwood accept a consolidated invoice for joint deals or do you require separate customer contracts?
[09:05] Sofia: Typically Redwood invoices the end-customer directly. For revenue share we do partner settlement. If you need consolidated invoicing that's possible but requires a setup with finance - we can scope that after initial deals.
[09:20] Raj: Ok, we'll flag if consolidated invoicing is necessary for any P0.
[09:27] [09:40] Diego: Two quick technical flags I want to add: 1) Model quantization options affect latency/cost tradeoffs and we need to choose the quant level for each POC; 2) For RAG pipelines, vector DB choices matter—we can recommend hosted Pinecone or self-managed Weaviate depending on the customer's preference.
[09:58] Lena: One of our customers uses an internal vector store, prefer self-managed. Can Redwood integrate with that?
[10:03] Diego: Yes, we can route retrieval calls to your vector store via a connector; we'll include connector docs.
[10:10] [10:20] Maya: Okay let's go through the eight-opportunity prioritization quickly—Priya can assign P0/P1, but we should all agree on the top three to run immediate engagement.
[10:30] Priya: Top three: Alpha (manufacturing) P0, Beta (healthcare) P0, Gamma (retail) P1. Alpha has exec sponsor; Beta has heavy compliance. Gamma is easier but lower ACV.
[10:43] Maya: We'll recommend running Alpha and Beta in parallel with slightly different technical skews—Alpha show low-latency Dedicated, Beta show compliance + guarded RAG.
[10:55] Tom: For resourcing, do you expect a dedicated AE to be assigned per deal or can we co-own across the same Redwood AE?
[11:02] Maya: We usually assign one Redwood AE per account for quota clarity; co-assignment credits will be configured in SFDC so Astradyne reps get attribution.
[11:12] Priya: Fine.
[11:14] [11:30] Sofia: Ops action: I'll create the shared SFDC fields and a partner folder with the playbook, cheat sheets and slide deck.
[11:38] Raj: Sounds good.
[11:40] [11:50] Diego: One more thought on competitive positioning—Anthropic is hyper-focused on safety messaging, Cohere pitches easier developer SDKs; Vertex AI is strong on cloud integrations. We should map our differentiators per account.
[12:05] Maya: Agreed. We'll add a competitor mapping section for each prioritized deal so sales can tailor messaging.
[12:12] Priya: Can you also include a one-liner battlecard for each competitor?
[12:16] Maya: Yes, short battlecards will be in the playbook.
[12:21] [12:30] Tom: Timeline check—what are we committing to for next week?
[12:33] Maya: Joint demo for Alpha—target demo date 2025-08-26. Playbook + spreadsheets out by 2025-08-22. Diego bench results by 2025-08-26. SFDC fields live by 2025-08-24. Exec alignment call by 2025-08-28.
[12:50] Priya: Those dates work for us.
[12:53] [13:00] Maya: Anything else from Astradyne?
[13:03] Raj: Maybe just one ask: can you provide a short note describing the expected timeline for Dedicated provisioning? Our legal will ask.
[13:10] Diego: Provisioning timeline: for Dedicated with reserved capacity we usually need four to six weeks for capacity and networking validation; with pre-existing templates (and if they accept reserved commit) can be closer to three weeks. We'll detail prerequisites.
[13:26] Priya: Helpful.
[13:28] [13:40] Lena: For the technical demo, we'll need a data schema primer from Redwood to map to our customer's doc format.
[13:47] Diego: I'll send a short mapping doc and an example ingestion pipeline.
[13:52] Priya: Great.
[13:55] [14:00] Maya: Ok I'll close—recap of next steps in the chat and I'll attach the playbook. Thanks everyone.
[14:07] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward to the playbook.
[14:10] Tom: Thanks.
[14:12] [14:15] Meeting end

Action items (recap):
- Maya: Playbook, pricing bands, partner cheat sheet (due 2025-08-22)
- Diego: Latency/cost bench and POC eval snapshot, mapping doc (due 2025-08-26)
- Sofia: SFDC co-sell fields and shared folder (due 2025-08-24)
- Priya: Prioritized opportunity list + contacts (due 2025-08-25)

References/links mentioned: co-sell playbook (to be attached), lead routing spreadsheet (to be shared), security pack (SOC2 link), sample connectors doc (to be attached)

Transcript notes: auto transcription, occasional mishears: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash", "Dedicated" sometimes appears as "dedicated capacity" or "dedicated deployment".
